sections.heading: Core Gameplay Mechanics
sections.body:
The core gameplay mechanics of Sun in Space are simple yet challenging. Your goal is to collect as many suns as possible while avoiding deadly planets. The game is played on a 2D plane, with the yellow square representing your character. You can move the square around the screen using your mouse or keyboard. The planets are constantly moving, and you need to time your movements perfectly to avoid getting hit. The game also features power-ups that can help you survive longer and collect more suns. These power-ups can be obtained by collecting certain suns or by completing specific challenges.

The game also features a scoring system, where you earn points for collecting suns and surviving longer. The scoring system is based on a combination of factors, including the number of suns collected, the time survived, and the number of power-ups obtained. The game also features a leaderboard, where you can compare your score with other players. The leaderboard is ranked based on the highest score, and it's a great way to compete with other players and improve your skills.

One of the unique features of Sun in Space is its use of gravity. When you collect a sun, you'll notice that the yellow square will pull towards it.
